## Knatware LLM Notebook Generator

**Before using this workflow:**
1. (Optional) Authenticate the 5 Hugging Face API calls this workflow makes — see the **Hugging Face Auth (optional)** note near those nodes for exact steps. Unauthenticated works fine for public models, just with lower rate limits.
2. If you plan to use **"Upload to Google Drive & open in Colab"**, open the **Upload to Google Drive** node and connect a Google Drive OAuth2 credential (Anthropic/Claude cannot create this credential for you — it must be authorized inside your own n8n instance).
3. (Optional) If you want generated notebooks to auto-login with a Hugging Face token, see the HF_TOKEN_CONSTANT comment block at the top of the **Fill Notebook Template** node's code.
4. Activate the workflow, then open the Step 1 form's production URL to run it.

**Flow:** Step 1 (search) -> live Hugging Face model dropdown -> Step 2 (pick model) -> live Hugging Face dataset dropdown filtered by that model's task/family -> Step 3 (pick dataset) -> Step 4 (hyperparameters + delivery choice) -> notebook is generated -> Download **or** pushed to Drive with a ready-to-open Colab link.

## Hugging Face Auth (optional)

The 5 HTTP Request nodes calling huggingface.co ship with **Authentication: None** — this works fine for public models/datasets, just with Hugging Face's lower unauthenticated rate limit.

To authenticate them (needed for gated models like Llama/Gemma, or to raise the rate limit), on **each** of the 5 nodes:
1. Open the node, set **Authentication** to **Generic Credential Type**.
2. Set **Generic Auth Type** to **Header Auth**.
3. Create/select a credential with **Name** = `Authorization` and **Value** = `Bearer <your Hugging Face token>`.

Why not an environment variable? Many self-hosted n8n instances set `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE`, which denies workflows any `$env` access at all — a real, common security policy, not a bug in this workflow. n8n Credentials aren't affected by that setting, which is why this workflow uses them instead. See README_Notebook_Generator.md > "Secret / constant parameters" for the full explanation.

parameters.formDescription: Step 1 of 4: find a base model. We'll query Hugging Face live and let you pick from real results (or type your own model id) on the next page.

values.html: Search Hugging Face for a base model to fine-tune. Leave the search box blank to see the most-downloaded models. (Your Hugging Face token is configured once by an administrator as a secret — it isn't collected here.)

values.hint: Used later to suggest repo/Space names. You can leave this blank and fill it in on the last step instead.

values.placeholder: e.g. llama, qwen, mistral, gemma, phi

values.option: Small (up to 3B - best for free Colab)

parameters.formTitle: Step 2 of 4: Choose Your Base Model
parameters.formDescription: Pick a model from live Hugging Face results, or override with any repo id.

parameters.formTitle: Step 3 of 4: Choose Your Training Dataset
parameters.formDescription: Ranked by relevance to your chosen model, then by popularity. Override with any dataset id if you prefer.

Every field is pre-filled with a recommendation shown as placeholder text. Leave a field blank to accept it, or type your own value. Choose how you'd like to receive the finished notebook at the bottom.
